title: Migrate async trait families from async-trait macro to native AFIT
description:
## Why

MSRV was raised 1.73 -> 1.87 in Nov 2026. async-fn-in-traits (AFIT) stabilized in Rust 1.75, so the `async-trait` macro is no longer required.

PKIX-a1yc.10 chose `async-trait` for pkix-revocation-http's AsyncRevocationFetcher / AsyncRevocationChecker with an explicit MSRV rationale: 'async-trait used (MSRV 1.73 precludes native async-fn-in-traits).' That rationale has expired. The workspace Cargo.toml comment on the async-trait pin (line ~188) still frames it as a workspace-level pin for pkix-revocation-http only.

Each `#[async_trait]` method boxes its future as `Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send + 'async_trait>>` — one heap allocation per call. Negligible next to a network round trip, but unnecessary.

## Doc/impl mismatch to fix alongside

pkix-revocation-http/src/async_fetcher.rs:44-45 already DOCUMENTS the trait surface as returning `impl Future + Send`:

    //! The trait surface here is runtime-agnostic — it returns
    //! `impl Future + Send`. Consumers drive the futures with their chosen

The code uses `#[async_trait]`, which boxes instead. The doc describes the shape native AFIT would actually give. Either the doc is wrong today or it is describing the post-migration state; migrating makes it true.

## Scope

- pkix-revocation-http — AsyncRevocationFetcher, AsyncRevocationChecker (landed, PKIX-a1yc.10)
- pkix-dane-resolver — AsyncTlsaResolver (not yet written; see PKIX-j32w.2)
- pkix-aia-http — async family if/when it lands

## Trade-off that must be decided before migrating

Native AFIT traits are NOT dyn-compatible: `&dyn AsyncRevocationChecker` stops compiling. async-trait's boxing is what makes it object-safe today. Before migrating, confirm whether any consumer or internal path needs dynamic dispatch over these traits. If yes, options are (a) stay on async-trait, (b) keep native AFIT and ship a boxed `DynAsyncX` adapter wrapper, (c) native AFIT plus an explicit `-> Pin<Box<dyn Future>>` method for the dyn path.

pkix-chain is generic (static dispatch) over the sync seams, so the sync side is not affected either way.

## Why filed rather than done inline

Decided 2026-11-24 (Mark, interactive) while designing pkix-dane's resolver seam: pkix-dane-resolver will use async-trait for now so the DANE crates stay uniform with pkix-revocation-http. The async idiom is a workspace-wide decision and must not fork per-crate — a new crate is the wrong place to unilaterally switch idioms. This bead is where the workspace-wide switch happens, all crates at once.

## Acceptance

[ ] dyn-compatibility question above answered and recorded
[ ] async-trait removed from workspace Cargo.toml (or its remaining use justified)
[ ] async_fetcher.rs:44-45 doc claim matches the implementation
[ ] All feature combos green (cargo hack --depth 2), clippy clean, rustdoc -D warnings clean
design: async-trait for now; native AFIT workspace-wide in one sweep, not per-crate. Dyn-compatibility loss is the gating question.
notes:
Raised 2026-11-24 during PKIX-j32w.1 design discussion. MSRV 1.87 per AGENTS.md non-negotiable #4.

HISTORY CORRECTION (2026-11-24, Mark recalled, verified against git): the AFIT blocker was real, not a preference. At PKIX-a1yc.10 time the workspace MSRV was 1.73, BELOW the 1.75 where async-fn-in-traits stabilized, so async-trait was the only option available.

Crucially, the unblocking was INCIDENTAL. MSRV rose 1.73 -> 1.87 in commit 5a3ed995 ('feat!: move to x509-cert 0.3, der 0.8, spki 0.8 and RustCrypto 0.14', Nov 2026 wave) because the new crypto stack demanded it -- crypto-bigint 0.7, elliptic-curve 0.14, rsa 0.10, x509-ocsp 0.3. Nobody raised MSRV in order to get AFIT. That is why the async idiom was never revisited: the constraint lifted as a side effect of an unrelated dependency upgrade and no bead was watching for it.

So this bead is not 'the rationale expired' -- it is 'a blocker silently cleared and nothing noticed'. Worth checking whether other decisions were parked on MSRV 1.73 and are now similarly unblocked without anyone having looked.
